cells.tense: You can take in the whole shape of a thing and set it down clearly.
cells.act: attend to the one thing that is asking for attention and leave the rest
cells.ask: Find the single matter that is genuinely asking for you this week, and give it what you've got. Let the others wait. Nothing else has to change.
cells.core:
You can hold the whole shape of something and not get lost in it. Standing inside a situation, you see how the parts lean on each other, and you can lay that out for people in a way they can use. The answer doesn't have to come first. What matters arrives before you've worked out why, and you're easy enough with that to start anyway.

The clearest signal comes when you're not trying to hold everything at once. Find the single matter that is genuinely asking for you and give it what you've got. Let the others wait. They will keep. Start with what matters and trust the order to show itself after.
cells.sheetLine: You can name the shape of it before you can explain it.
cells.verb: Building the frame that lets the complexity move
cells.place: standing outside the pattern while still inside it

cells.tense: You're building the frame before the thing it holds has arrived.
cells.act: trace the pattern across the last few times
cells.ask: Trace how the same pattern has shown up lately — one line, nothing more. No fixing. Leave it for a week and watch what loosens when you stop tightening.
cells.core:
You're organizing something that hasn't arrived. The structure gets heavier, the sequence more fixed, the rule outgrows what it was made to carry. It feels like staying ahead. From where others stand it reads as brace — you're setting the shape before the shape is ready. What you built to hold the work is crowding the work out.

Trace how the same pattern has shown up lately — one line, no detail, nothing to fix. Then leave it. A week of watching will tell you whether the arrangement can carry weight without your grip on it. A frame can hold and still stay open at the ends; what's coming will find somewhere to land.
cells.sheetLine: The tighter the frame, the less it holds.
cells.verb: Building the frame that lets the complexity move

cells.tense: You've been standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.act: stand in the gap it leaves without rebuilding yet
cells.ask: Let one old sequence go — the plan you keep reordering in your head. Then stay with what the ending opens. Rebuild nothing yet. No clock on this.
cells.core:
The pieces don't assemble right now. There's too much on the table and no order that holds, so the sequence shifts and the priority slides and the whole thing runs a step behind where you actually are. What you're carrying is a plan for a version of this that's already finished. The door is behind you and you're still at it.

Let one of those sequences go — the plan you keep reordering in your head — and stay with what the ending opens. Rebuild nothing yet. The ground the next structure needs gets cleared by something ending, not by something starting. You'll know the difference between an old plan closing and a new one opening before either one is built.

cells.tense: You're drawing the lines the room is moving by, and asking where the drawing came from.
cells.act: let the old form go so the next one can come
cells.ask: Name what people rely on you for — how you've sorted it, the order it flows in. Say it once and keep the name. That's all.
cells.core:
People keep coming to you for the order of things, and you keep answering, and the answer keeps working — and you still feel like you're making it up as you go. The organizing happens. Your name isn't on it. You file the structure under circumstance, or under somebody's request, and from where you stand there's no shape at all.

Name what people rely on you for — how you've sorted it, the order it moves in. Say it once and keep the name. Naming it is the ending of an old form and the beginning of the next. The form was yours, and you get to carry it as yours without anyone else's say.
cells.sheetLine: Others build on your order. It was yours.
